claim: claude -p "prompt" runs Claude Code non-interactively; it exits 0 on success and non-zero when the run fails, so scripts can branch on exit status.
quote: Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails, so your scripts can branch on the exit status.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Failures inside a run (e.g. missing auth) are printed as the result on stdout, not stderr; invalid flags are reported on stderr before the run starts.
quote: When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Data can be piped on stdin to claude -p; stdin is capped at 10MB (larger input should be a file referenced in the prompt).
quote: Piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: The official docs show a shell script taking a positional argument ($1) and piping data into claude -p with --append-system-prompt and --output-format json.
quote: In the script, "$1" stands for the first argument you pass on the command line. Run bash review.sh 123 and the shell replaces "$1" with 123 , so the script fetches the diff for PR 123.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: --bare skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md; it is recommended for scripted calls, will become the default for -p, and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (no subscription login).
quote: --bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Without --bare, claude -p runs project hooks and connects .mcp.json servers with no trust dialog or per-server approval, even in an untrusted folder.
quote: A -p session shows no workspace trust dialog and no per-server approval prompt.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Output formats are text (default), json (result, session ID, metadata) and stream-json (newline-delimited); --json-schema with json puts schema-conforming data in structured_output, which may be absent so scripts must check.
quote: If a run ends without valid structured output, for example because Claude declined the request, the response has no structured_output field.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: stream-json needs --verbose, and --include-partial-messages for token deltas; json output includes total_cost_usd (client-side estimate).
quote: Use --output-format stream-json with --verbose and --include-partial-messages to receive tokens as they’re generated.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: In v2.1.302+ a claude -p run with no permission mode set starts in Manual mode, where calls needing approval are denied unless allowed by --allowedTools, a PermissionRequest hook or --permission-prompt-tool.
quote: In a Manual mode claude -p run, a call that needs approval is denied unless something approves it, such as a PermissionRequest hook or a --permission-prompt-tool .
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: --permission-mode accepts default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions (manual alias); dontAsk denies every call that would otherwise prompt.
quote: dontAsk : Claude Code denies every call that would otherwise prompt, which is useful for locked-down CI runs
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: --permission-prompts none (v2.1.259+) denies anything that would prompt and tells Claude not to retry; denials appear in permission_denials of the final result.
quote: Anything that would prompt is denied unless a PermissionRequest hook allows it, Claude is told that nobody can approve the request and not to retry it, and the run continues.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: --allowedTools uses permission rule syntax; trailing space-star gives prefix matching, e.g. Bash(git diff *).
quote: The space before * is important: without it, Bash(git diff*) would also match git diff-index .
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: --dangerously-skip-permissions is equivalent to --permission-mode bypassPermissions.
quote: Skip permission prompts. Equivalent to --permission-mode bypassPermissions .
title: CLI reference

claim: --max-turns limits agentic turns (print mode only) and errors when reached; no limit by default.
quote: Limit the number of agentic turns (print mode only). Exits with an error when the limit is reached. No limit by default.
title: CLI reference

claim: --max-budget-usd caps estimated spend (print mode only), is checked against a client-side estimate, and can be exceeded.
quote: Claude Code checks the cap against its client-side cost estimate , which can differ from your bill.
title: CLI reference

claim: Session continuation: --continue/-c (most recent in cwd), --resume/-r with ID or name, --fork-session, --session-id (UUID), --no-session-persistence (print only); session_id is read from json output with jq.
quote: session_id = $( claude -p "Start a review" --output-format json | jq -r '.session_id' )
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Plain --continue skips sessions created by claude -p; claude -p --continue includes them. Parallel/repeated runs therefore should use explicit session IDs.
quote: Skips sessions created with claude -p or the Agent SDK, and sessions whose first prompt was /loop . claude -p --continue includes -p , SDK, and /loop sessions.
title: CLI reference

claim: System-prompt flags: --append-system-prompt(-file) adds to default; --system-prompt(-file) replaces it.
quote: Load additional system prompt text from a file and append to the default prompt
title: CLI reference

claim: In -p mode, user-invoked skills/custom commands work when /skill-name is included in the prompt string; terminal-only built-ins like /login are unavailable.
quote: User-invoked skills and custom commands work. Include /skill-name in the prompt string and Claude Code expands it before running.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: --model takes an alias or full name and overrides the model setting and ANTHROPIC_MODEL; --fallback-model gives an ordered fallback chain.
quote: Overrides the model setting and ANTHROPIC_MODEL
title: CLI reference

claim: SIGTERM on a claude -p run exits with code 143 and records no result for the in-progress turn.
quote: Claude Code exits with code 143.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: A claude -p run may stay open waiting for background work; default cap is 10 minutes idle, adjustable with CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS.
quote: To change the 10-minute cap, set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS , or set it to 0 to wait without one.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Practitioner pitfall (self-reported by search snippet, not fetched): denied tool calls in claude -p can still give exit code 0 and is_error false; check permission_denials in JSON output.
quote: claude -p returns exit code 0 , "subtype": "success" and "is_error": false even when Claude never touched a file. The only trace is the permission_denials array in the JSON
title: Claude Code Hub: dangerously-skip-permissions silent failure
